note: Section 8: full memory accounting for the --gpu-layers N mechanism used in Sections 9-11, making explicit the weight-vs-KV split that architecture.json's critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling flags -- this mechanism moves BOTH weights and KV per layer, not KV alone. All numbers real, from membrane-run --json's own gpu_policy/storage fields plus external nvidia-smi (same runs as vram_reduction.json).

decomposition_of_the_measured_vram_savin.note: the arithmetic sum of independently-computed weight and KV savings (196.9 MiB) matches the directly measured external VRAM delta (199 MiB) to within ~2 MiB (~1%), which is within the noise band this phase has seen elsewhere (e.g. Phase 11E's overhead_calibration.json) -- the saving is FULLY explained by these two additive components, no unaccounted memory.

honest_takeaway: roughly HALF of the VRAM savings this phase measured and reported in vram_reduction.json/second_model.json/pressure_test.json comes from moving LAYER WEIGHTS off GPU (a well-understood, pre-existing llama.cpp capability, not novel to this phase), not from KV cache placement specifically. The KV-specific portion is real and substantial on its own (95.6 MiB out of 199 MiB at this scale), but reporting the COMBINED number as if it were a pure KV-tiering win would overstate what this phase's own mechanism actually isolates. See architecture.json for why decoupling the two (moving ONLY KV, keeping weights GPU-resident for fast compute) requires a llama.cpp patch this phase does not write.
